comments.author: Jon D. (Overcat)
comments.content:
Regarding null:

I think the default type might expand proportionally to the complexity of the world model if null != false.  After all, you'd have to explicitly set new properties to false in the default type as the model grew.

What are some of the foreseeable drawbacks of equating null to false in expressions?

comments.author: Alex Warren
comments.content: A drawback I see is that it makes it impossible to tell if the object actually has a null value for a boolean, or if it's genuinely a boolean false.

comments.author: Jon D. (Overcat)
comments.content: Hmm.  Perhaps it is best to leave the two as distinguishable.  I guess that's why you have Quest defining the IsNull function?

comments.author: Alex Warren
comments.content: Actually that info on the wiki is out of date - there's no IsNull function any more. You can just check for equality with null as normal, e.g. "if (object = null) ..."
